query: Turning the Fever Charm {A first-year in the end bed has a fever, and the cooling charm over the bed has to be turned by hand every hour until dawn. Sister Amaranth looks at you, then at the chair.|Another fever, another chair. The cooling charm's brass ring is worn smooth where hands turn it.|The chair by the end bed. Sister Amaranth has left a cushion on it, which is as close as she comes to asking.} {The ward is quiet except for the clock.|Rain is drumming on the infirmary roof.|{season == "winter": Frost feathers the window behind the bed.|Moths keep the lamp company.}} Take the night watch {You turn the ring every hour and watch the fever ebb by inches. At dawn Sister Amaranth says "Keep doing that," and takes the chair.|You doze between turns and wake on the hour, every hour, as if the ring calls you. The patient wakes clear-eyed. You don't.|You know the charm's weight now and turn it half asleep. At dawn the patient asks your name. You're too tired to remember it.} Promise next time, and sleep {Sister Amaranth turns the charm herself, without comment, and that's worse than a comment.|You go to bed and lie awake a while, counting hours you're not turning.|You leave the cushion on the chair for someone else. You sleep, mostly.}
